subject: orders.py:9
title: average_price divides by zero on empty input
detail:
graded A: reproduced, backed by a runnable artifact, survived falsification.

average_price(prices) computes total/len(prices) with no check that prices is non-empty; order_summary calls it with prices derived from order["items"] which could be an empty list.

No guard exists for the empty-list case, so an order with zero items causes ZeroDivisionError instead of a sensible summary (e.g. average 0.00 or 'no items').

Strongest case against: One could argue this is "intended behavior" in the sense that an order with zero items is a degenerate/invalid state that should never occur in the real system (e.g., upstream validation guarantees items is non-empty before order_summary is called), making the crash an acceptable fail-fast signal for a data-integrity violation rather than a bug to fix defensively. If that invariant is enforced elsewhere, average_price's lack of a guard would be a non-issue in practice.
